description:
Prerequisite split out of joinorder-canonical-validation-test-coverage w0
(2026-07-03 re-review). The canonical IMDb 2013 data has LEGITIMATE dangling
references -- FKs are opt-in metadata, not load-time constraints
(benchbox/core/joinorder/schema.py:67-68). A full-archive FK
referential-integrity test therefore needs to pin WHICH (fk_table, fk_column,
parent_table) pairs legitimately dangle and by how much, so corruption is
distinguishable from known-source noise.

Verified 2026-07-03: no such committed artifact exists. The build pipeline
has FK closure machinery only for tiny-fixture construction
(_project/scripts/build_joinorder_data.py:265 ForeignKey,
:2651 close_tiny_ids_over_foreign_keys); nothing under _project/joinorder/
names the full archive's legitimate dangling set. Hand-deriving that policy
inside an integration test is forbidden by the parent seed's guardrails --
it must be a durable, reviewed, re-runnable artifact.

anti_patterns.dont: hand-write the allowed-dangling set from spot queries
anti_patterns.why: it must be generated by a committed, re-runnable script against the hash-verified archive.
per-FK counts (and parent/child table names) are sufficient and keep the artifact compact and reviewable.

preserves.behavior: The artifact records the manifest data_archive_hash it was generated against, so a future dataset version cannot silently reuse a stale dangling census.
benchbox/core/joinorder/ ships no new runtime dependency on the artifact -- it is a build/test-side reference, like reference_cardinalities.json.

prior_art.concept: _project/joinorder/reference_cardinalities.json -- the committed-oracle precedent (provenance header + hash-locked to the dataset) this artifact should follow.
_project/scripts/build_joinorder_data.py:1191 postgres_foreign_keys, :2651 close_tiny_ids_over_foreign_keys -- existing FK declarations and closure machinery to reuse.
benchbox/core/joinorder/schema.py:67-68 -- documents that dangling references are legitimate and FKs are opt-in.

verifications.command: uv run -- python -c "import json,pathlib; a=json.loads(pathlib.Path('_project/joinorder/allowed_dangling_fks.json').read_text()); print(bool(a['data_archive_hash']) and len(a['foreign_keys'])>0)"
verifications.description: Artifact exists, parses, and is hash-locked to the manifest
Regenerating the census against the same archive is idempotent

work_units.notes:
Extend _project/scripts/build_joinorder_data.py (or a sibling script)
with a subcommand that, for every declared FK in the JOB schema
(reuse postgres_foreign_keys() at :1191 or the schema_specs.yaml
declarations), counts child rows whose non-NULL FK value has no parent
row, over the sha256-verified full archive (DuckDB over the Parquet files
is sufficient; no Postgres container required). Emit a compact JSON
artifact under _project/joinorder/ (e.g. allowed_dangling_fks.json)
recording per-FK dangling counts plus the manifest data_archive_hash it
was computed against.

DONE 2026-07-10: added the `fk-dangling-census` subcommand to
build_joinorder_data.py. FKs are sourced from schema_specs.yaml (via
JoinOrderSchema, no Postgres container); dangling counts are computed with
DuckDB LEFT JOIN anti-matches over the sha256-verified shipped Parquet
(fetched via JoinOrderBenchmark.generate_data()). Emitted
_project/joinorder/allowed_dangling_fks.json (27 FKs; hash-locked to
manifest data_archive_hash 0f9061ba...). Result: a single legitimate
dangling FK, aka_title.movie_id -> title.id (93 rows, 1 distinct missing
title); all 26 other declared FKs are fully closed. Cross-checked the 93
via NOT EXISTS and EXCEPT ALL; NULL counting validated against the
in-repo CANONICAL_NULL_COUNTS oracle.
work_units.summary: Generate the allowed-dangling FK census from the canonical archive

work_units.notes:
Human-review the census (sanity: dangling sets concentrated in the
known-noisy IMDb link/info tables; zero dangling where the schema
guarantees closure), then commit it alongside a short provenance note
(generator command, archive hash, date) following the
reference_cardinalities.json precedent.

DONE 2026-07-10: committed _project/joinorder/allowed_dangling_fks.md
(generator command, archive/manifest hashes, date, review findings)
alongside the JSON, following the reference_cardinalities.json precedent.
Review note: the census is MORE closed than the seed anticipated -- the
only dangling FK is aka_title.movie_id (93 rows), and every
closure-guaranteed relationship/dimension FK is zero. That is consistent
with schema.py:67-68 (dangling references legitimate but rare in the
Dataverse restore); the 93 aka_title rows point at one absent title id, a
minor source artifact, not corruption.
work_units.summary: Review and commit the artifact with provenance

work_units.notes:
A small _project/scripts function (this seed's scope_limit excludes
tests/) that loads the artifact and verifies its recorded
data_archive_hash against the manifest. The downstream FK integration
test (joinorder-canonical-validation-test-coverage w2, which owns
tests/) consumes the reviewed set through it -- or through its own
trivial JSON load of the committed artifact -- instead of embedding
policy.

DONE 2026-07-10: added load_allowed_dangling_fks() in
build_joinorder_data.py -- it loads the committed JSON and raises if the
artifact's data_archive_hash no longer matches the shipped manifest
(stale-census guard). The downstream FK integration test can consume it,
or do its own trivial JSON load + manifest hash check per the seed's
allowance (that test owns tests/; this seed's scope excludes it).
work_units.summary: Expose a loader helper for tests
